- Expunge/compaction: background sweep runs can permanently remove payloads between 7–30 days; customers can request an expedited sweep for emergency erasure (requires an elevated ops run and approved change window).
- Evidence: we can provide a manifest showing snapshot IDs and object indexes, DR sweep logs, and a signed attestation from Redwood confirming the expunge run and KMS key states.

Hi all — technical detail below (keeping it high-level for sharing with the customer; happy to provide deeper notes under NDA):

How deletion propagates
- Control plane delete => primary metadata marked deleted instantly; object tombstones written to metadata store.
- Tombstones are streamed to replicas via CDC pipeline; under normal load that stream reaches all in-region replicas within minutes and is reflected in backup manifests within 24 hours. Cross-region async replication depends on queue depth — typical window 24–72 hours.

Expunge / sweep behavior
- We run continuous minor compaction tasks; a major expunge (payload-level removal) runs hourly in a staggered fashion but will only pick up objects eligible past the configured retention/hold period. Default internal expunge policy removes orphaned payloads after 7 days in test regions and 30 days in production by default.
- For emergency erasure, we have an "expedite expunge" ops playbook: schedule a targeted expunge run for the affected shard(s) and mark snapshots as superseded; this is expected to complete within 48 hours for a scoped, single-customer request (depends on dataset size).

Evidence we can provide
- Snapshot manifest (JSON): lists snapshot id, object index hashes, and tombstone markers.
- DR sweep logs: timestamped entries for compaction and object purge.
- KMS key activity: records of key rotation/deprecation tied to object encryption contexts (note: we don't delete keys unless requested; key destruction is a separate compliance action).

Sanitized exemplar attachments attached: redwood-backup-manifest-2025Q3.pdf (sanitized manifest), dr-sweep-log-20250712.txt (sample sweep log).

If you want a signed attestation, we can generate one after we run the targeted expunge — that attestation will reference the manifest IDs and the expunge job id.

—Rishi
